results.content: Home » AI To Produce 90% Of News By 2026? # AI To Produce 90% Of News By 2026? In 2022, warnings that 90% of online content could be AI-generated by 2026 caused concern across media companies. Halfway through 2025, here’s what media executives have learned about separating hype from newsroom reality. Three years ago, a viral prediction sent shockwaves through media boardrooms: “90% of online content will be AI-generated by 2026.” Major outlets from Futurism to Yahoo Finance amplified the claim, attributing it to a report from the European law enforcement agency, Europol. Law enforcement and the challenge of deepfakes” instead focuses specifically on deepfake technology’s impact on law enforcement and criminal activities, not AI content generation forecasts. Research from Futuri’s “AI in Media Study” found that 45% of local TV news viewers believe AI could help present better stories, and 79% might or would trust AI-generated content when sourced from a local news website or a local TV station and delivered by a human.

results.title: Why LLMs fail science — and what every CPG executive must know | CIO
results.content: # Why LLMs fail science — and what every CPG executive must know. ## AI’s great at sparking ideas, but in CPG, only real-world testing proves what works — and that’s where the winners will stand out. It’s no surprise that business leaders are asking: *If an AI can write a convincing research paper or simulate a technical conversation, why can’t it run scientific experiments?* In some circles, there’s even a whispered narrative that scientists — like travel agents or film projectionists before them — may soon be “disrupted” into irrelevance. As someone who has spent over two decades at the intersection of AI innovation, scientific R&D, and enterprise-scale product development, I can tell you this narrative is both dangerously wrong and strategically misleading. No, they cannot replace the process of scientific experimentation — and misunderstanding this boundary could derail your innovation agenda, especially in industries like Consumer Packaged Goods (CPG) where physical product success depends on rigorous, reproducible, real-world testing. But here’s the rub — formulation is science, and science is not a language game.
